headline: Highest risk is medium: MemMachine’s MCP/networked context can amplify prompt injection and data leakage, while awesome-python is non-runnable and mostly inert.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, so it can ingest external content through shared channels; if awesome-python content is copied into that flow, instruction-like text could be misread. awesome-python itself is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it is not an active injector. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF MemMachine ingests content from awesome-python via MCP, REST, or SDK without provenance filtering, injection risk exists.
IF the operator manually copies repository text into MemMachine prompts, attacker-controlled instructions can be followed.
mitigations: Disable direct ingestion of repository text into MemMachine prompts.
Add a provenance tag to any copied content before review.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from pasted text.
Review MCP tool outputs before acting on them.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance checks.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context and can egress over allowlisted network paths, so sensitive context may leave the local boundary. awesome-python touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not a leakage source. The pairwise risk is mainly that MemMachine can transmit user context if connected to shared inputs; this is plausible in default integrations, so medium fits.
conditions: IF MemMachine receives user conversations containing sensitive facts, those facts may be sent over allowlisted egress.
IF the operator connects shared workspace content into MemMachine, that content can enter its context window and be transmitted.
mitigations: Do not route sensitive notes into MemMachine.
Restrict allowlisted destinations to required endpoints only.
Clear conversational context before handling sensitive tasks.
Separate repositories from agent prompts.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on outbound requests.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write, network, or mutable-resource permissions, while MemMachine has allowlisted egress and MCP/API access. There is no evidence of overlapping write scopes, shared filesystem writes, or locking conflicts. Because the pair lacks a documented shared mutable resource, conflict is limited and low.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory or API resource, conflicts can emerge.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locks, concurrent updates may collide.
mitigations: Keep awesome-python read-only.
Avoid giving MemMachine write access to shared files.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Add explicit locking if shared state is introduced.
requires-engineering: implement concurrency control for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can act on conversational context and external API/MCP inputs, so if it treats copied content from awesome-python as authoritative, downstream mistakes can propagate. awesome-python is a static collection, not a verifier, so it cannot correct MemMachine’s assumptions. The pathway exists by inference rather than direct evidence, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF MemMachine uses text copied from awesome-python as factual guidance, it may propagate errors.
IF MemMachine takes action based on unverified repository snippets, downstream outputs can be wrong.
mitigations: Require human verification before action-taking.
Treat repository text as untrusted reference material.
Ask MemMachine to cite source lines before use.
Use a second pass to check factual claims.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before external actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class is explicitly present in either profile, and awesome-python has no data handling. MemMachine does retain conversational context and long-term user facts, so compliance concerns are possible if regulated data is entered, but the profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch. Only MemMachine is relevant here, so one citation suffices.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is entered into MemMachine, retention and residency policies must be checked.
IF the operator requires deletion/export guarantees, MemMachine’s handling must be validated first.
mitigations: Avoid entering regulated data.
Review MemMachine retention settings.
Document deletion/export procedures.
Limit stored context to non-sensitive facts.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls with policy.
